title: Two-Rule Bit Flips Down to Zero
statement:
You have a non-negative integer n written in binary, with bit 0 as the lowest bit. In one move you may do exactly one of these:

  • Flip bit 0.
  • Flip bit i (for i ≥ 1), but only if bit i − 1 is 1 and every bit below i − 1 is 0.

Return the fewest moves needed to turn n into 0.

examples.why: 10 → 11 (flip bit 0) → 01 (bit 1 may flip because bit 0 is 1) → 00. Bit 1 cannot be cleared directly.
101 → 111 → 110 → 010 → 011 → 001 → 000. Clearing bit 0 first (to 100) looks like progress but leads to 100, which alone needs 7 moves.

hints: Try small cases by hand. How many moves does it take to clear a single set bit 2^k?

Clearing 2^k alone takes 2^(k+1) − 1 moves: the moves walk through every value below 2^(k+1). For a general n with top bit k, think of it as the walk from 2^k, shortened by the moves you get for free from the lower bits.
f(n) = (2^(k+1) − 1) − f(n XOR 2^k). Unrolled, this is n XOR (n >> 1) XOR (n >> 2) XOR …, the inverse Gray code.

explain.intuition:
Only two moves are ever possible from a nonzero value: flip bit 0, or flip the bit just above the lowest set bit. So the values form a single long path, and this path is exactly the Gray code sequence: neighbours differ in one bit. Reaching 0 from n means walking back to the start of that sequence, so the answer is the position of n in Gray code order.

Converting a Gray code value back to its position is a classic trick: XOR together n, n >> 1, n >> 2, and so on. Seen recursively: a lone bit 2^k needs 2^(k+1) − 1 moves, and for n with top bit k, the lower bits m = n XOR 2^k are already part of the way, so f(n) = 2^(k+1) − 1 − f(m).
pitfalls: Counting set bits, or summing 2^(k+1) − 1 over each set bit. The bits interact: 3 needs only 2 moves, not 1 + 3.
Searching with BFS. The answer can be close to 2³¹, so you would visit billions of states.
Using - instead of XOR when unrolling the recursion; the alternating signs only line up as XOR.

solutions.title: Breadth-first search over values
solutions.idea: From any value there are at most two moves: flip bit 0, or flip the bit above the lowest set bit. BFS until 0 is reached.

solutions.title: Recursion on the top bit
solutions.idea: Clearing 2^k alone costs 2^(k+1) − 1 moves. With lower bits m present, f(n) = 2^(k+1) − 1 − f(m).

solutions.title: Inverse Gray code
solutions.idea: The moves walk the Gray code sequence, so the answer is the position of n in it: n XOR n>>1 XOR n>>2 XOR …

followups: Go the other way: given a number of moves m, which value do you reach from 0 after exactly m moves along the shortest path?
What is the fewest moves to turn a into b instead of into 0?
